metadata.title: The a0 Law with Cold Dark Energy Counted Once: the Form the Record Closes On, Its Gates, and What Stays Open (Working Note)
metadata.description:
Working note, version 1.2 (2026-11-12; v1.1: DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24125791). AI-assisted research programme; not peer reviewed; not reproduced by any outside group. kappa = 1/2 is fitted; the theory is not closed; nothing here says the data favour this framework.

This note states the form on which the record closes and grades it. It does not complete the theory. The a0 law alone fails the CMB, the growth of structure, clusters and the Bullet, each for want of the same cold, clustering component of about 5.4 times the baryons. Every way tried of keeping that component out of galaxies has a failing verdict; the last one is recorded here. The form chosen by the owner on 2026-11-09 counts the component once: it is in galaxies too, and around condensed baryons the law describes how it sits. It is real mass, not a second force. In the adopted action this is the static state's own reading: the law's halo is the khronon sector's energy density, carried by the one conserved charge that is dust in the expanding background. We regrade the form with criteria frozen before any number. On groups and clusters it is not falsified, by a gate that can fail from one side only, and the richest clusters sit at its ceiling; the Bullet passes only if the subcluster's stripped gas is counted. On hosted dwarfs it fails: it removes most of the law's shortfall in every class, but two classes stay high and four low rows cannot be reached. On KiDS lensing by galaxy type the test returns no verdict; its readings put early types between the law and the form's truncated halo and cannot place discs; on host-free lenses the form passes a gate that does not separate it from the law. The form passes rotation curves. Its CMB, lensing and growth rows hold when computed, on an amended reading of that lane's checks. With the amplitude of fluctuations pinned by large-angle polarisation, CMB lensing matches the prediction to 0.3 sigma and the growth rate passes. Raw KiDS weak lensing, on a gravity-only spectrum, prefers an amplitude five of its own widths lower: the absolute fit is excluded at 3 sigma by the frozen line and reads tension once the reference run's realisation noise is corrected, a check made after grading. This is the tension that any cold component fitted to the CMB carries; the form states neither gas ejection nor neutrino mass, and does not relieve it. With gravity coupled the static state is linearly stable around a point mass; an instability found earlier belonged to a planar background.

Version 1.1 adds the lanes that landed on 2026-11-10 and states the theory in six rules (Section 7). The collapse was computed and breaks down: a clock that starts as dust folds at the centre, and the equations give no answer beyond that moment. The static state is stable around isolated discs away from their centres; a disc in an external field has no verdict, with stability excluded there, and a disc's own centre is open. No dust term tried, keyed on the clock's offset, on its expansion or on its acceleration, joins the falling state to the standing one; the clock's leafwise flux cannot supply the halo; and the action has no cluster state at the form's own dust constant. A survey of media with more structure than one clock finds no class without a failing verdict. On the data side, most of the weak-lensing gap was the survey's superseded release and our own inputs: on KiDS-Legacy, with a neutrino floor, the covariance at the model and the reference run's draw corrected, the form's amplitude sits 1.71/1.88 of the survey's widths high with an acceptable fit, while DES Y3 stays at 2.18/2.23 on a re-scanned fit. These readings rest on post hoc amendments: the lane's amended label is GAP STAYS and its frozen labels are NO VERDICT. With fixed-amplitude reference runs spliced in at low k, an interim reading on one full-size pair puts DES Y3 at 1.85/1.83 and both surveys inside two widths; that lane's frozen label is NO VERDICT, and its amended label, graded after version 1.1 on two full-size pairs, reads AMPLITUDE CONSISTENT, is post hoc and awaits an independent re-grade. The two failing dwarf classes do not survive the record's own systematics budget, and a gas-history reading does not explain them. The form's data rows are computed without the joint between its two states, and several of them fail or have no verdict. The form is not complete.

Version 1.2 adds the lanes that landed after version 1.1 (Section 8). The Lyman-alpha forest row, computed for the first time at the forest's own redshifts, FAILS on both footings (Delta chi^2 9916/9009 against a line of 4); an independent blind build of the same row also FAILS, no a0 that changes with redshift passes, and one history of the settled radius leaves no window between the forest and galaxy lensing, though a blind re-grade of that lensing gate returns no verdict. At the level of the transmitted flux, two independent builds of the forest row both return NO VERDICT as frozen. The flux is less sensitive than the matter-level projection because the mass the law moves sits in saturated gas; the blind build's reported reading still misses the line by about a hundred times, and the first build's much smaller miss rests on a pressure-smoothing scale about four times the published one. No lane finds the joint between the falling and the standing clock, derives kappa or the share 5.41, or identifies the medium, and no lane turns a failing gate into a pass; the lanes whose labels read as passes are listed as awaiting an independent re-grade or together with their blind re-grade. We list what is open, the measurement that would decide each item, and our own wrong estimates.

The supplement zip holds every committed file of the lanes the note cites (criteria, amendments, scripts, outputs, mutation outputs, results, and Lean files where a lane has them) and the owner's decision file; version 1.1 adds the lanes of 2026-11-10, the two notes of that day with the check script and its output, the re-run record, and the result files of the older lanes quoted in Section 7.
